objective: Explore the pokeemerald repository structure to understand the codebase layout, key systems, and build configuration — mapping major source directories, identifying promising systems to hack (wild encounters, starters, trainer battles), and recording findings in memory files to establish a foundation for future cycles.
reasoning: This is cycle 1 with zero prior knowledge. Before making any changes, a solid mental model of the codebase is needed. Research mode is the right call — explore directory structure, read key files like the Makefile and main entry points, scan src/ and data/ to understand how game systems are organized. This groundwork will directly inform what kind of ROM hack is feasible and where to start. No code changes should be made this cycle; the output should be rich memory files that future cycles can build on.
summary: Explored the pokeemerald codebase comprehensively. Mapped all major directories and systems: 313 C source files, battle engine (60+ files), wild encounters (JSON data + C logic), starter selection (simple 3-element array), Pokemon data structures (4-substruct encrypted format), build system (agbcc classic vs arm-gcc modern). Recorded all findings in 4 memory files.

objective: Change the starter Pokémon from Treecko/Torchic/Mudkip to an unexpected trio (Larvitar, Bagon, Beldum) by editing the sStarterMon[] array in src/starter_choose.c, then build to verify the change compiles successfully.
reasoning: Cycle 1 established a solid foundation of codebase knowledge. Strategy notes explicitly recommend Cycle 2 as the starter change — it's the lowest-risk, highest-impact first modification: a pure data change to three constants in a single array. The target file is known (src/starter_choose.c, sStarterMon[] array), the build system is well-understood, and a successful build will validate the end-to-end patch workflow. Choosing Larvitar/Bagon/Beldum as pseudo-legendary starters gives the ROM hack a distinct identity — three Dragon/pseudo-legendary lines with Rock/Dragon/Steel typing, creating a thematically coherent "Legends" starter experience that diverges sharply from vanilla Emerald.
summary: Changed starter Pokémon from Treecko/Torchic/Mudkip to Larvitar/Bagon/Beldum by editing sStarterMon[] in src/starter_choose.c (lines 113-118). Build succeeded — pokeemerald.gba produced with no errors.

objective: Expand the wild encounter overhaul to cover all major routes across Hoenn in a single comprehensive pass — designing a thematically coherent regional ecosystem where each area has distinct, non-vanilla Pokémon that fit both the 'Legends' aesthetic and the geography, from Routes 103–134 through Victory Road and key dungeons.
reasoning: Cycles 2 and 3 established the foundation: pseudo-legendary starters and early-route encounter overhauls on Routes 101/102. But doing routes one or two at a time is too slow — a complete encounter overhaul across all of Hoenn in one feature cycle is both achievable (the JSON format is well-understood) and far more impactful. Players should feel the 'Legends' identity from Route 101 all the way to Victory Road, with escalating rarity and power as they progress. This cycle will design and implement the full encounter table using thematic groupings by geography (rocky routes get Rock/Ground types, water routes get sea monsters, caves get eerie/dark Pokémon, late-game routes get near-legendary species), creating a cohesive alternate Hoenn. This is the centerpiece feature of the ROM hack and should be done ambitiously rather than piecemeal.

Geographic theming: volcanic routes get Magmar/Arcanine, desert gets Larvitar, rivers get Dratini, ice coasts get Lapras, final ocean routes have Dragonair dominance with Milotic as ultra-rare. objective: Implement the comprehensive rival team overhaul for Brendan/May across all their battle encounters — designing escalating teams where the rival's pseudo-legendary starter (counter to the player's choice) evolves through each fight, supported by increasingly powerful teammates that create memorable, challenging battles throughout the Hoenn journey.

With gym leaders now using powerhouse teams, the rival battles would feel anticlimactic with their vanilla Treecko/Torchic/Mudkip progression.
